answer: A reputation system assigns each agent a trust kernel that grows with verified task completions and decays during inactivity. New identities start at zero reputation, making them unable to access high-value work—the pearl opportunities reserved for aged accounts. An attacker spinning up fresh agents on island nodes faces prohibitive cost: each sybil must execute months of low-paid tasks to build credibility before earning enough to recoup creation expenses, and any detected fraud resets the entire investment to zero.
